source.title: Meta-Unlearning on Diffusion Models: Preventing Relearning Unlearned Concepts
source.authors: Hongcheng Gao; Tianyu Pang; Chao Du; Tai-Hang Hu; Zhi-Jie Deng; Min Lin

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some table formatting is flattened, making the Table 1 pre-finetuning values difficult to assign reliably; those values are not used below.
record.tranche_reason: Tests relearning after unlearning in text-to-image diffusion models, a different modality from the LLM settings in the claim, using malicious and benign fine-tuning datasets.
record.gate_note: The study measures nudity scores after fine-tuning unlearned and meta-unlearned diffusion models. Table 1’s pre-finetuning values are not assigned because the flattened layout is unclear. The study does not test ablation, quantization, or prompting-only attacks. It cites prior language-model studies but those cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Tests fine-tuning relearning of unlearned concepts in text-to-image diffusion models (SD-v1-4, SDXL), a different modality from the LLM originals. Nudity score is the percentage of nude images on I2P nudity prompts; the original SD-v1-4 scores 97.18. Six unlearning methods are fine-tuned on harmful (HRM-s, HRM-m) and benign (CLEAN) sets. The study also proposes a counter-method (meta-unlearning, F) and reports one adversarial-prompt attack (UnlearnDiffAtk) on RECE. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude meta-unlearning keeps benign quality while 'largely reducing' (not eliminating) relearning of unlearned concepts after malicious FT. They also say it preserves, rather than improves, RECE's adversarial robustness.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces meta-unlearning: existing diffusion-model unlearning objectives are augmented with a meta objective intended to impede later fine-tuning-based relearning. It is not a replication of the cited LLM unlearning methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Fine-tuning dataset changes the measured nudity scores: harmful HRM-s/HRM-m and benign CLEAN conditions differ. The study also evaluates multiple unlearning methods; meta-unlearning’s reductions vary by method and dataset.
record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV), as stated in the supplied record
record.problems: The experiments concern diffusion models rather than LLMs. The numerical primary measure is nudity score, not targeted-knowledge accuracy. The text does not state the number of images in each fine-tuning dataset. Table 1’s flattened pre-fine-tuning values cannot be reliably assigned; the selected post-fine-tuning scores are legible in the reported sequence. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Fine-tuning is the only recovery attack tested.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 results for 50, 200, and 300 fine-tuning steps are omitted to stay within the row limit while retaining the 100-step comparisons across all six unlearning methods and all three datasets. Table 3’s Unsafe score and NSFW score results, Table 1’s pre-fine-tuning values, and qualitative image panels in Figures 2–5 and 10–11 are not separately extracted. The additional 100-step-variation/300-step material appears in Table 1 and Appendix B, and qualitative examples appear in Sections 5.1–5.3 and the appendices.

untested.parts: LLM setting; targeted-knowledge accuracy against chance; attacks other than fine-tuning and one adversarial-prompt attack.
LLM setting; relearning on unrelated data beyond the CLEAN set; dataset sizes not stated.
Not tested: no activation ablation, no analysis of blocking versus deletion.
Only UnlearnDiffAtk on RECE. No rephrasing, other languages or in-context information; no LLMs.
No quantization, ablation or prompt-attack resistance claimed. LLMs not tested.

missing.what: UnlearnDiffAtk attack success rate: RECE unlearned 64.79% vs RECE meta-unlearned 62.68%
Before-FT nudity values (original 97.18; unlearned and meta values), assignable from the flattened Table 1
Qualitative SDXL relearning of copyright (SpongeBob, Snoopy) and style concepts after 100 FT steps; meta-unlearned resists
Sensitivity of post-FT nudity to γ1:γ2 ratio (21.13–28.17) and inner steps M (26.76→32.39)

record.verdict_notes: Every HRM-m row used 200-step values while being labelled 100 steps. r15, r16, r27 and r28 took values from wrong cells; r25 and r26 took 200-step values. All rows needing correction are listed above. Diffusion nudity score is a proxy for targeted-knowledge recovery, not LLM knowledge accuracy. Small gaps between conditions have no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: Tests recovery after fine-tuning for diffusion models, but does not measure targeted-knowledge accuracy against chance; does not test the claim across LLM methods or simple attacks other than fine-tuning.
Uses fine-tuning on harmful prompts and a benign dataset, but does not establish that the image training set is small or test fine-tuning on a subset of forgotten facts in the sense of the claim.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis showing that unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
No prompting-only recovery attack, rephrasing, jailbreak, language variation, or in-context recovery.
Tests meta-unlearning against fine-tuning on the tested datasets only; does not test resistance to ablation, quantization, or prompting-only attacks.

source_check.notes: Table 1 is flattened but recoverable: 12 method rows x 12 columns, and the Before FT column lists 97.18 then 12 values in row order. Many rows use 200-step cells for 100-step conditions, and baselines are stated. Nudity values move in steps of about 0.70 points, likely 142 images (inferred, not stated), so changes like 3.52->4.93 are about 2 images. The text does not state the venue (arXiv v2, Aug 2025).

statements.problem: Gives no number for this study. Its direction (harmful forget-concept data recovers more than benign data) holds here. Cited r03 and r27 hold wrong cells; they are fixed at row level.

statements.correction: SD-v1-4 diffusion model, not an LLM. Benign CLEAN FT, 100 steps: ESD-u-1 6.34->13.38, RECE 4.93->9.86; original SD 97.18. Other methods: SDD 1.41->16.20, UCE 16.90->25.35, ESD-u-3 3.52->4.93.
statements.problem: Cites this study under 'LLM knowledge', but it is SD-v1-4 nudity unlearning. 'Weak recovery' fits the cited ESD-u-1 and RECE CLEAN rows. Cited r25 holds the 200-step cell.

statements.correction: 100 steps: RECE 4.93->19.72 (HRM-m), 14.79 (HRM-s); ESD-u-1 6.34->21.83 (HRM-m), 24.65 (HRM-s). At 300 steps: ESD-u-1 HRM-s 53.52, RECE 22.54. Original 97.18.
statements.problem: 'Little or no recovery' overstates for ESD-u-1 and only loosely fits RECE. Both rise severalfold under harmful FT; the authors call the rise rapid.

statements.problem: Numbers right at 100 steps. 'Slow relearning little or not at all' overstates: meta roughly halves 100-step nudity for most methods. The gap is weak only for SDD on HRM-m.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Standard unlearned SD-v1-4 methods after 100 steps of fine-tuning on HRM-m or HRM-s
reader_labels.reason: Nudity scores after malicious fine-tuning are reported for the standard unlearned models, and the authors describe recovery of harmful-image generation; see r01, r03, r05, r07, r09, r11, r13, r15, r17, r19, r21, and r23. The study does not establish the chance-level starting accuracy part of this version.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Standard unlearned SD-v1-4 methods after fine-tuning on HRM-m or HRM-s for 100 steps
reader_labels.reason: The study reports nudity scores after target-related malicious fine-tuning and states that standard unlearned models relearn harmful-image generation; the result is not shown to be complete restoration to the original model, so it is partial. See r01, r03, r05, r07, r09, r11, r13, r15, r17, r19, r21, and r23.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Standard unlearned SD-v1-4 methods after benign CLEAN fine-tuning for 100 steps
reader_labels.reason: Some nudity scores are reported after benign fine-tuning, and the authors state unlearned models may still generate harmful images, but the scores are generally lower than after harmful fine-tuning and the study does not establish restoration of the original capability. See r25, r27, r29, r31, r33, and r35.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Meta-unlearned SD-v1-4 models fine-tuned for 100 steps on HRM-m, HRM-s, or CLEAN
reader_labels.reason: Across the reported method/dataset conditions, meta-unlearned models have lower nudity scores than their corresponding unlearned models under the same fine-tuning condition. See r02, r04, r06, r08, r10, r12, r14, r16, r18, r20, r22, r24, r26, r28, r30, r32, r34, and r36.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The meta-unlearned models’ reported scores remain nonzero in the listed conditions, so the experiments show reduced recovery rather than its elimination; the paper also tests only fine-tuning, not the other attacks in the claim. See r02, r04, r06, r08, r10, r12, r14, r16, r18, r20, r22, r24, r26, r28, r30, r32, r34, and r36.
